l4_steps.name: Define fare class hierarchy in PSS
l4_steps.input: Fare product strategy brief, IATA booking class standards
l4_steps.output: Booking class configuration (Y, B, M, H, K, Q, V, W, L, G) in PSS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active fare products mapped to a booking class within 2 business days of product launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa booking class table has finite slots; adding new classes for ancillary bundles requires PSS configuration freeze that blocks concurrent distribution updates

l4_steps.name: Map booking classes to RM fare buckets
l4_steps.input: Booking class list from Altéa, revenue segmentation guidelines
l4_steps.output: Fare bucket mapping table in NRM linking each booking class to O&D revenue tier
l4_steps.kpi: Zero mismatches between Altéa booking class codes and NRM bucket definitions at go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM fare bucket schema uses internal numeric IDs that do not auto-sync with Altéa booking class labels; manual reconciliation required after each PSS config change

l4_steps.name: Validate fare class structure against ATPCO rules
l4_steps.input: NRM bucket mapping, published ATPCO fare records (Records 1, 2, 3)
l4_steps.output: Validation report confirming booking class eligibility rules match ATPCO Cat 25 combinability and Cat 5 advance purchase restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: 0 ATPCO rule violations flagged by GDS edits at filing; audit pass rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 25 combinability rules interact with NRM bucket nesting in non-obvious ways; misalignment causes ghost inventory — classes show available in GDS but are blocked in NRM

l4_steps.name: Publish fare class availability to GDS channels
l4_steps.input: Validated booking class configuration, SSIM schedule file
l4_steps.output: Live availability display in Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS for all market O&Ds
l4_steps.kpi: GDS availability refresh latency ≤ 90 seconds from NRM availability change; GDS parity rate ≥ 99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre GDS availability cache TTL (up to 90 s) creates window where high-demand bucket closures are not yet reflected, enabling over-sell of discount classes during flash sales

l4_steps.name: Extract historical O&D booking data by fare class
l4_steps.input: Altéa booking history (24 months), departure date range for planning horizon
l4_steps.output: O&D booking curve dataset segmented by fare class, day-of-week, and booking lead time
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction covering ≥ 95% of historical departures within planning window; query SLA ≤ 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-COVID booking patterns (2021–2022) distort historical curves; including them without seasonality dampening causes demand models to under-forecast leisure peak

l4_steps.name: Run demand forecast model per O&D bucket
l4_steps.input: Historical booking curves, competitive fare inputs from OAG Schedule Analyser
l4_steps.output: Forecast demand curve per fare bucket per O&D, including unconstrained demand estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast MASE (Mean Absolute Scaled Error) ≤ 0.25 for 90-day horizon; unconstrained demand estimate within ±12% of actuals at departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM's detruncation algorithm underestimates unconstrained demand on routes with chronic sell-outs; results in systematic under-forecasting for high-yield buckets

l4_steps.name: Review forecast variance and approve bucket plan
l4_steps.input: NRM forecast output, analyst commentary on anomalous markets
l4_steps.output: Approved demand forecast for bucket sizing; markets flagged for manual review escalated
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast review cycle ≤ 48 hours before system-generated availability updates are applied; < 5% of markets requiring manual correction
l4_steps.pain_point: High analyst workload during peak schedule planning cycles forces rubber-stamping of model outputs; errors not caught until post-departure revenue review

l4_steps.name: Set initial bucket inventory levels for departure
l4_steps.input: Approved demand forecast, aircraft capacity from Amadeus SkyMAX fleet assignment
l4_steps.output: Initial bucket protection levels and booking limits per fare class per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Bucket initialisation completed ≥ 330 days before departure for all long-haul markets; ≥ 90 days for short-haul
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX fleet assignment changes propagate to NRM with up to 6-hour lag; bucket limits set against wrong aircraft type cause premature close-out of discount classes

l4_steps.name: Configure EMSR-b bid price and nesting strategy
l4_steps.input: Approved bucket protection levels, fare class revenue values, willingness-to-pay estimates
l4_steps.output: Bid price thresholds and virtual bucket nesting hierarchy loaded into NRM for each O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price calibration complete ≥ 180 days before departure for long-haul; revenue uplift from nesting vs. partitioned control ≥ 2% RASM on calibrated markets
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM's EMSR-b calculation does not natively account for ancillary revenue (bag fees, seat upgrades) in WTP estimates; bid prices structurally undervalue leisure segments

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking pace against expected S-curve
l4_steps.input: Real-time bookings from Altéa, expected booking curve from NRM forecast
l4_steps.output: Booking pace index (BPI) per flight per fare class; pace alerts for flights deviating > 20%
l4_steps.kpi: BPI monitored at T−90, T−60, T−30, T−14, T−7, T−3 checkpoints; alert resolution SLA ≤ 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM booking pace alerts have a minimum 15-minute polling interval; during flash sales or news events, early-warning signals arrive too late to prevent discount class oversell

l4_steps.name: Adjust bucket thresholds based on pace deviation
l4_steps.input: Booking pace alert, current bucket availability, revised demand estimate
l4_steps.output: Updated protection levels and booking limits; change log entry in NRM audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Bucket adjustment applied within 2 hours of pace alert; average revenue recovery per adjustment ≥ $8/seat on affected flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent intraday bucket adjustments on the same flight trigger NRM re-optimisation queue delays; changes queue behind batch jobs and may not take effect for up to 30 minutes

l4_steps.name: Open or close fare classes per booking curve triggers
l4_steps.input: NRM availability recommendation, time-to-departure trigger rules
l4_steps.output: Updated fare class availability in Altéa and reflected across GDS/NDC channels
l4_steps.kpi: Availability update propagated to all GDS endpoints within 90 seconds; close-out of discount classes ≥ T−3 on flights with load factor forecast ≥ 90%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway availability sync with Altéa runs on a separate thread from GDS availability; NDC channel may display open discount inventory up to 3 minutes after GDS close-out

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time bookings and cancellations by class
l4_steps.input: Live Altéa booking stream, cancellation and refund events
l4_steps.output: Real-time seat availability dashboard; auto-triggered re-open events when cancellations create sell-up opportunity
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue recovery from cancellation-triggered re-opens ≥ $15/seat; dashboard refresh ≤ 5-minute lag vs. Altéa booking engine
l4_steps.pain_point: High-volume cancellation events (weather, IROPS) flood NRM with availability change events; system enters degraded mode and availability updates queue, causing stale GDS displays

l4_steps.name: Process group booking requests against bucket availability
l4_steps.input: Group booking request (≥10 pax), current bucket availability, group fare contract
l4_steps.output: Group PNR with blocked inventory or counter-offer at higher fare class
l4_steps.kpi: Group booking response time ≤ 24 hours; group revenue contribution ≥ 8% of total flight revenue on managed markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa group booking module holds seats as option status for up to 72 hours; large group holds on high-demand flights suppress availability for individual high-yield bookings, eroding RASM

l4_steps.name: Review exception queue for manual intervention flights
l4_steps.input: NRM exception queue (special events, comp schedule changes, distressed inventory flags)
l4_steps.output: Prioritised list of flights requiring analyst action; override justification form initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Exception queue reviewed twice daily (09:00 and 14:00 local); < 3% of managed flights in exception state at any time
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM exception queue intermingles flights flagged by automated rules with analyst-generated annotations; high-priority items can be buried under system noise during IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Apply manual bucket override with audit justification
l4_steps.input: Approved override justification, competitor fare filing from OAG Schedule Analyser, event calendar
l4_steps.output: Manual availability override applied; audit log entry with approver, rationale, and expected revenue impact
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of manual overrides documented in NRM audit trail; post-event review shows manual overrides outperform model recommendation in ≥ 60% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM audit trail does not capture the external data (event calendars, competitor filings) that justified the override; institutional knowledge lost when analysts turn over

l4_steps.name: Generate post-departure revenue performance report
l4_steps.input: Altéa final booking close-out file, NRM forecast at departure, actual revenue by fare class
l4_steps.output: Post-departure report: RASM, load factor, yield, and spill/spoilage by bucket for each departed flight
l4_steps.kpi: Report generated within 48 hours of departure; RASM variance between actual and pre-departure NRM estimate reported for 100% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa close-out files arrive in S3 in variable formats depending on PSS version; ETL pipeline requires manual intervention approximately 3% of the time due to schema drift

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate NRM forecast model parameters
l4_steps.input: Post-departure performance reports (rolling 13 weeks), MASE trend, spill and spoilage analysis
l4_steps.output: Updated NRM model parameters; recalibration change log; improvement targets set for next review cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Quarterly recalibration reduces MASE by ≥ 0.02 vs. prior quarter; spill rate ≤ 3% and spoilage rate ≤ 5% on managed O&Ds post-calibration
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM model recalibration requires a 72-hour training window during which live availability recommendations revert to static rules; scheduling this window without impacting peak sale periods is operationally difficult
